description: This file defines classes and methods for managing job execution, including job counters, job clients, and GNU make job server integration. It handles process spawning, environment setup, and file descriptor passing for concurrent job control.

classes.name: JobHandle
classes.description: A small object to handle claiming and releasing a job.

classes.name: JobClient
classes.description: Abstract base class for job clients, providing methods to get jobs, environment variables, and start subprocesses.

classes.name: GNUMakeJobClient
classes.description: A job client for GNU make, managing job server communication and process control.

classes.name: GNUMakeJobServer
classes.description: Implements a GNU Make POSIX job server, extending GNUMakeJobClient.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Constructor for JobHandle, initializes with a release function and arguments.

methods.name: __enter__
methods.description: Context manager entry method for JobHandle (no implementation).

methods.name: __exit__
methods.description: Releases the job by calling the release function with stored arguments.

methods.name: get_job
methods.description: Claims a job, returning a JobHandle object.

methods.name: env
methods.description: Returns environment variables needed for job sharing.

methods.name: pass_fds
methods.description: Returns file descriptors to pass to subprocesses.

methods.name: popen
methods.description: Starts a subprocess with given arguments, setting environment and file descriptors.

methods.name: from_environ
methods.description: Creates a GNUMakeJobClient from environment variables, parsing MAKEFLAGS for job server info.

methods.name: get_job
methods.description: Claims a job by waiting for readiness on selectors and reading from file descriptors.

methods.name: env
methods.description: Returns environment variables for GNU make job server.

methods.name: pass_fds
methods.description: Returns file descriptors to pass to subprocesses.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Initializes a GNUMakeJobServer, setting up pipes and writing initial tokens.
